trends.what: A curated list of free public APIs for developers to use in their projects.
trends.why: It's the ultimate reference for developers looking to quickly integrate third-party data or services without reinventing the wheel.

trends.what: An open-source platform offering a full curriculum to learn coding, math, and computer science for free.
trends.why: It remains a go-to resource for self-taught developers, and its massive community keeps it constantly updated and relevant.

trends.what: A massive collection of freely available programming books and learning resources in multiple languages.
trends.why: It democratizes access to technical knowledge, making it a staple for anyone learning to code on a budget.

trends.what: A personal AI assistant that runs on any OS and platform, designed to be fully customizable and private.
trends.why: The idea of a self-hosted, cross-platform AI assistant is resonating as users seek more control over their AI tools.

trends.what: Interactive roadmaps and guides that help developers navigate career growth and skill progression.
trends.why: With tech careers evolving fast, developers are hungry for clear, structured paths to learn new skills and stay competitive.

trends.what: A tool that makes AI agents write code like a lazy senior developer, favoring minimal and simple solutions.
trends.why: It's a humorous yet practical take on reducing over-engineering, which resonates with devs tired of bloated AI-generated code.

trends.what: A fullscreen, mouse-interactive terminal UI harness for coding agents, designed for extensibility and power users.
trends.why: As AI coding assistants become mainstream, developers want more immersive and controllable interfaces, and this fills that niche.

trends.what: Runs frontier mixture-of-experts AI models on existing hardware by streaming experts from disk, with zero dependencies in pure C.
trends.why: It promises to make high-end AI models accessible on consumer hardware, which is a huge draw for hobbyists and researchers on a budget.
